title: Telco Customer Churn — Prediction, Causal Validation, and Experimentation
subtitle: H2O AutoML, Bayesian causal correction, and a hierarchical A/B engine
status: As-built — dashboard deployed to Google Cloud Run
summary: A five-phase system that moves from churn prediction to causal validation to prospective experimentation. The predictive phase reaches 93.4% AUC-ROC with an H2O stacked ensemble; the causal phase catches and corrects a collider-bias error that had understated the effect of service add-ons by an order of magnitude; the experimental phase designs three randomized tests at 95% Bayesian power with sequential monitoring.
problem: A churn model tells you who is likely to leave but not what to do about it. Acting on predictive feature importance as if it were causal is the standard failure mode and produces retention programs that spend money without moving the metric. This system separates the two questions explicitly, and in doing so surfaces a conditioning error that would have led to abandoning a lever that actually works.
goals: Predict churn accurately enough to prioritize retention outreach.
Estimate the causal effect of service add-ons under a defensible identification strategy.
Design randomized experiments where observational data cannot identify the effect.
Deploy a stakeholder-facing dashboard for the Bayesian results.
non_goals: Automated retention offers driven by model score.
Real-time scoring — the pipeline is batch.
Transferring the estimates to a real telco; the data is fictionalized.
requirements: Causal estimates must satisfy the backdoor criterion
Met — adjustment restricted to exogenous pre-treatment demographics only
Met — 95% Bayesian power, stratified randomization, ROPE-based stopping rules
Sequential monitoring without inflating error rates
Met — hierarchical Bayesian A/B engine with ROPE stopping
Met — Streamlit dashboard on Cloud Run
Snapshot data with no event log — churn timing unrecoverable
Accepted; this is precisely why tenure behaves as a collider

data.sources: Kaggle / IBM Telco Customer Churn — 7,043 customers × 21 features, 26.54% churn rate
data.pipeline: PySpark EDA in Phase 1; SMOTE for class balance before H2O AutoML; causal phases read the raw table directly with restricted adjustment sets.
data.notes: TotalCharges is stored as TEXT because 11 rows hold a blank string — all 11 are tenure-0 customers, exactly the population the early-tenure hypothesis concerns. Service columns encode 'No internet service' as a third level (21.67% of rows), which creates collinear indicators if one-hot encoded without collapsing.

candidates: H2O AutoML Stacked Ensemble (GBM + XGBoost + GLM)
Bayesian model conditioning on tenure, contract, payment method
Rejected — tenure is a collider, contract and payment are co-treatments
Bayesian model on exogenous pre-treatment demographics only
selected: H2O stacked ensemble for prediction; a demographics-only Bayesian specification for causal estimation; three prospective randomized experiments for everything the observational data cannot identify.
selection_rationale: The correction is the centerpiece. Conditioning on tenure seems natural — it is the strongest correlate of churn — but tenure is caused by both add-on adoption and churn, so conditioning on it opens a non-causal path. This was confirmed empirically via stratification reversal. Moving to an exogenous-demographics-only adjustment set shifts the estimated add-on effect from −0.2pp to −5.8pp: the naive specification would have led to killing a lever that works. Where even the corrected model cannot identify an effect — notably the +52pp early-tenure signal — the answer is an experiment, not a better regression.

evaluation.strategy: Train/test split with SMOTE applied to training only for the predictive phase. Causal phases do not split — they estimate on the full table under a declared identification strategy, then hand off to prospective randomized tests. Phase 4 monitors those tests sequentially with ROPE-based stopping.
evaluation.baseline: PySpark Decision Tree (72.0% AUC) for prediction; the collider-biased specification (−0.2pp) as the cautionary causal baseline.
metrics: 3 tests at 95% Bayesian power; Week 6 winner at 99% confidence

dataflow: Raw Telco CSV → PySpark EDA → engineered features
features + SMOTE → H2O AutoML → stacked ensemble → Models/
raw table + exogenous demographics → PyMC → corrected causal estimate
causal estimate → power analysis → stratified randomization → assignment logs
experiment data → hierarchical Bayesian engine → sequential decision memos

deployment.current: The Phase 5 Streamlit dashboard is containerized and deployed to Cloud Run in us-central1 via deploy_to_cloud_run.sh, with a dedicated Dockerfile and requirements.txt under 'Phase_5_Depolyment guide'. DEPLOYMENT.md documents the procedure. The modeling and causal phases are not served — they run offline and write results that the dashboard reads.
deployment.gaps: No scoring API — the ensemble is not served, only its results are displayed. H2O models require a JVM at serving time, which is why they are not behind the dashboard. Experiment assignment logs are CSVs in the repo rather than in a durable store. Directory name 'Phase_5_Depolyment guide' contains a typo that will break naive path handling.

monitoring.current: Phase 4 is a genuine monitoring system: the hierarchical Bayesian engine evaluates running experiments sequentially against ROPE-based stopping rules and generates automated decision memos. A Week 6 winner was declared at 99% confidence.
monitoring.gaps: This monitors experiments, not the model. There is no prediction drift tracking, no calibration check (SMOTE distorts predicted probabilities), no fairness monitoring across the demographic features that sit in both the feature and adjustment sets, and no retraining trigger.

risks: Demographics (gender, senior citizen, dependents, partner) appear in both the prediction and adjustment sets, so score-driven offers could distribute unevenly across protected groups
Demographics used as backdoor-criterion adjustment rather than targeting rules; the project routes decisions through stratified randomized experiments rather than model-score rollout.
Collider bias silently inverting effect direction
Detected, empirically confirmed via stratification reversal, and corrected — the documented centerpiece of the project.
Acknowledged; calibration assessment is a roadmap item.
Acting on the +52pp early-tenure signal without identification
Explicitly flagged as 'requires experiment'; three randomized tests designed at 95% power.
Predictive accuracy mistaken for causal validity
The five-phase structure exists specifically to keep these separate.

open_questions: Would a calibrated XGBoost pipeline match the H2O ensemble closely enough to drop the JVM dependency and make real-time serving practical?
The corrected add-on effect is −5.8pp with 87% probability of ≥5% reduction. Is that enough certainty to fund a rollout, or does it warrant the experiment first?
How much of the 93.4% AUC comes from features that are unavailable at decision time in a real deployment?
